title: Pointwise cocartesian transport of coherent diagrams
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories, right-pinched mapping spaces and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a map between quasicategories. Call an edge $u:x\to y$ over $f:p(x)\to p(y)$ cocartesian if, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the square with top row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$ given by precomposition with $u$ and bottom row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(p(y),p(z))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(p(x),p(z))$ given by precomposition with $f$ is a homotopy pullback. A homotopy pullback means that the map to the path-space homotopy fiber product is a weak homotopy equivalence. Suppose $p$ is an inner fibration (it lifts all inner horns) and every edge of $\mathcal B$ with source $p(x)$ has a cocartesian lift with source $x$.

For every small simplicial set $K$, postcomposition induces a cocartesian fibration $p_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$. An edge of its source is $p_K$-cocartesian if and only if its component at every vertex of $K$ is $p$-cocartesian. In particular, for $A:K\to\mathcal E$, $G:K\to\mathcal B$ and a coherent transformation $\eta:pA\to G$, there is a lift $\lambda:A\to\eta_!A$ with $p(\eta_!A)=G$ and cocartesian vertex components. Let $\mathcal F_G=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}\{G\}$ be the degreewise fiber. For every $H\in\mathcal F_G$, precomposition with $\lambda$ induces a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_G}(\eta_!A,H)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\eta}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(A,H)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(pA,G)\bigr).$$
Cocartesian lifts compose, and successive transports along composable coherent transformations agree, up to coherent equivalence, with transport along their composite. These equivalences are compatible with the displayed precomposition maps. If $G$ is constant at $b$, the fiber $\mathcal F_G$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_b)$. The case $K=\Delta^0$ gives the corresponding mapping-space fiber formula for objects of $\mathcal E$. No limits or colimits of $K$-diagrams are assumed.
